flashcard_questions.q: What is the formula for added value?

flashcard_questions.a: The difference between what a business pays for inputs and the price it charges.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the added value on a latte whose inputs cost £0.60 and which sells for £3.50?
What is the added value on a sausage roll costing £0.25 that sells for £1.20?
What is the added value on trainers costing £20 to make and selling for £110?
Which factor of production is the drive and motivation to start a business?
Which factor of production covers the money and equipment needed to start?
What is a unique selling point?
flashcard_questions.a: A feature that makes a product stand out from those offered by competitors.

flashcard_questions.q: Which smoothie brand adds value through natural ingredients with no added sugar?
Which clothing brand hand-crafts waxed jackets in the UK to add value through quality?
How does Amazon Prime add value for its customers?
Which slogan helps Nike charge a premium for its trainers?
How does McDonald's meet the customer need for speed?
flashcard_questions.a: Through its drive-thru and mobile ordering app.

flashcard_questions.q: How does Waitrose meet the customer need for quality?
flashcard_questions.a: It sells premium and locally sourced food.

flashcard_questions.q: What risk does an entrepreneur take before any sales are made?
flashcard_questions.a: Money is paid out in advance with no guarantee the product will sell.

notes: 15 cards: 1 formula card (added value), 3 one-step calculations using the lesson's own figures (latte £2.90, sausage roll £0.95, trainers £90), 3 term→definition, 2 factor-of-production classification cards, 6 concept→named example (Innocent, Barbour, Amazon Prime, Nike, McDonald's, Waitrose). The four factors of production and the five ways of adding value were not made into list cards.
